subject: Research artifact narrowed to editorial reading width — people-graph-360.html

body.summary: Narrowed the reading column on /research/people-graph-360.html from 760 px to 660 px, bringing it into Stripe Press / Bringhurst-aligned line-length territory (~70 chars at 17.5 px Newsreader). Recalibrated the matrix breakout column and footer column proportionally. Removed a dead CSS variable. This is the fourth pass on this artifact's width — the user's feedback was correct: 760 px was still too wide for a serious research piece.

changes.rationale: 760 px at 17.5 px Newsreader yields ~85-90 chars/line, which is newsletter width, not editorial. 660 px lands at ~70 chars — the Bringhurst-recommended range, consistent with Stripe Press and Linear changelog. The user said 'don't ship a tepid fix'; 660 is the honest number.

The competitor matrix uses a negative-margin breakout: margin = (col-read - col-mid) / 2. Keeping col-mid at 1080 while narrowing col-read to 660 would have expanded the breakout from 160 px/side to 210 px/side, making the matrix dominate the page. Narrowing to 940 keeps the breakout at 140 px/side — same ~21% extension ratio as before.

The footer at 1380 px was sprawling relative to a 660 px reading column. 1200 px brings the footer closer in, reducing the felt gap between content and chrome. The 5-column footer grid still has adequate air at 1200 px.
Dead variable. Defined in :root, referenced nowhere in the stylesheet. Cleaned up.

4.6 rem was set when the reading column was wide enough to carry it. At 660 px, 4.6 rem would overflow its column at mid-range viewports before the fluid vw value scaled down. Ceiling lowered to 3.6 rem — a serious research headline, not a display ad.

column_math.col_read: 660 px at 17.5 px Newsreader → ~70 chars/line at desktop
column_math.matrix_breakout: (660 - 940) / 2 = -140 px per side. Was -160 px at 760/1080. Same 21% extension ratio.
column_math.mobile_breakpoint: @media (max-width: 760px) retained — correct, it governs matrix card-stack collapse which is about viewport, not column width

tradeoffs: At very wide viewports (1920 px+) the footer at 1200 px still has significant margin on each side. Accepted — the reading artifact is a document, not a full-bleed marketing page.
The matrix at 940 px col-mid is narrower, which tightens the table cells. At 940 px all 12 vendors are still readable; the prose read column (last td) is the key one and it has overflow-wrap set.
body.o1_accessibility: Width change does not affect WCAG 2.2 AAA contrast. Narrower line length is a readability improvement — shorter line lengths reduce cognitive load for all readers, and are particularly beneficial for users with dyslexia or low vision. No AAA criteria regressed.
